messages:
ryan: Heads up — proposing a soft-unpin of runtime v3.2 for model newton-v1 in the EU canary window. We're seeing a longseq tokenization regression that affects generation correctness.

marta: Which regression exactly? perf or correctness?

ryan: Correctness. Reproducer below — whitespace tokenization causing stray insertions on prompts >2k tokens. Quick repro:```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://internal-eval/run -d '{"model":"newton-v1","runtime":"3.2","prompt":"<long prompt>"}' | jq .output```
logs: `gen_step(2048): token_id_mismatch at pos 1731`

samir: Can you paste a minimal reproducible snippet? Want to rule out KV cache warmup interplay.

ryan: Pasting short repro (sanitized):
```python
prompt = "A\n" * 2100
resp = client.generate(model="newton-v1", runtime="3.2", prompt=prompt)
print(resp.text[:400])
```
Behavior only on 3.2, not on 3.1.

marta: :eyes: @jen can QA run canary-suite diff (3.1 vs 3.2) on newton-v1, longseq tests?

jen: On it — kicking off suite now. ETA ~25m.

deploy-bot: pinlist check: runtime v3.2 rolled to canary (50%) in eu-west-1. No pin for model newton-v1.

ryan: Proposal: soft-unpin runtime v3.2 for newton-v1 for a 2h window starting 10:30 UTC (route newton-v1 to 3.1). This is a targeted soft-unpin (no global rollback). No infra changes. Objections?

samir: lgtm if QA confirms regression. Any impact on streaming endpoints?

ryan: Streaming unaffected; this is token selection. Still, watch for broken chat history tests.

marta: Dedicated customers? Sales says no EU dedicated users for newton-v1. Confirmed.

jen: QA report: run 12/12 longseq regressions triggered on 3.2 (examples attached to the ticket). 3.1 shows 0 regressions. I'm +1 for soft-unpin.

ryan: OK. I'll submit the deploybot job. Command I'm going to run:
```bash
deploybot soft-unpin --model newton-v1 --runtime 3.2 --fallback 3.1 --window 2h --start 2024-11-08T10:30:00Z --reason "tokenization regression longseq"
```

deploy-bot: soft-unpin scheduled. Job id: sb-20241108-77a9. Target: newton-v1 in eu-west-1 canary cohort. Will reroute to runtime 3.1.

ops-bot: scheduled action: soft-unpin(sb-20241108-77a9) queued for 2024-11-08T10:30:00Z. Health checks: will monitor error_rate (>0.5%) and latency (>p95 + 50ms) during window.

jen: Posting QA summary to ticket: short examples, diffs, and a recommended rollback threshold.

marta: Add release notes entry: "Temporary soft-unpin of runtime 3.2 for newton-v1 due to longseq tokenization regression; fallback to 3.1 while patching."

ryan: If things look worse we escalate to rollback by 11:45 UTC. Keep this thread for live updates.

qa-bot: smoke-suite after reroute: pass=94/96, fail=2 (non-critical formatting).

jen: After 15m: no increase in customer errors, latency stable. Still seeing some minor diffs in a small subset — filing a bug with research.

samir: Will open runtime kernel debugging ticket. Tentative fix path: adjust tokenizer merge logic and run golden tests.

ryan: Thanks — leaving monitoring flag on. I'll update when window closes or if rollback triggered. :thumbsup:

marta: Thanks team. Good call to soft-unpin targeted to the model.

ryan: Closing loop: window ended at 12:30 UTC, newton-v1 still routed to 3.1. Follow-up ticket for patch and re-roll scheduled.

deploy-bot: sb-20241108-77a9 closed — traffic restored to runtime 3.1 for newton-v1.

marta: Please add changelog note and link to bugfix PR when ready.

jen: Will attach QA artifacts and screenshots to the bug ticket.

samir: I'll assign myself on the kernel fix and ping here when PR is ready.

ryan: Nice work everyone. :tada:
